headline: 5-2 on 7 value plays, +$24.96
paragraphs: The model looked at 6 games in Week 4. It found a playable edge in 4 of them and left the other 2 alone. Those plays went 5-2, worth +$24.96 at $10 a play (35.7% on the $70 at risk).

By market, spreads went 2-0, totals went 1-2 and moneylines went 2-0. The best of them was Over 50 in Liberty at Coastal Carolina, a 5.5-point disagreement with the market that finished Liberty 34, Coastal Carolina 17. The one that stung was Over 48 in Army at Temple, a 8.5-point disagreement with the market that finished Army 21, Temple 17.

The five plays that actually got published went 0-1 for -$10.00, behind the full board. Ranking by expected value is supposed to concentrate the good ones at the top, and whether it does is something only a season of these will answer.

Season to date the model has made 7 value plays and gone 5-2, +$24.96 on flat $10 bets (35.7%). It expected to win 64% of those and won 71%. Treat all of it as early. At 7 plays the record is still mostly noise, and the thing worth watching is not the win rate but whether the market keeps moving toward these numbers.
